Page

bb_page.Rd

A page body is a vertical stack of blocks placed between the template's header and footer. Nothing needs a hand-set height: each block measures itself at the content width. Flexible blocks (plots without a height, [bb_spacer()]) share whatever height is left.

Usage

bb_page(
  ...,
  template = NULL,
  header,
  footer,
  gap = 0,
  data = list(),
  label = NULL,
  overflow = c("warn", "error", "ignore"),
  .list = NULL
)

Arguments

...

Body blocks (or anything [as_block()] accepts), top to bottom. `NULL`s are dropped.

template

A [page_template()]. Defaults to `page_template()`.

header, footer

Override the template's header/footer for this page (block, `function(ctx)`, or `NULL` for none).

gap

Space between body blocks, recycled.

data

Named values for `{name}` tokens and for header/footer functions.

label

Name used in overflow messages.

overflow

`"warn"`, `"error"` or `"ignore"`.

.list

Optional list of further body blocks.

Value

A `bb_page` object.

Details

If the content is taller than the space between header and footer, [export_pdf()] warns (or errors, with `overflow = "error"`) and says by how much.

Examples

pg <- bb_page(bb_section_header("Summary"), "Some text.", gap = 0.1)
